name: Jalam
title: Esau's son and Edomite tribal father
summary: Jalam was the second son of Esau and his wife Oholibama. He became a tribal chief in Edom and is counted among the forefathers of the Edomites. Although he does not play a prominent role in the biblical narrative, he is part of Esau's lineage that made up the people of Edom.

keyEvents.title: Jalam's birth in Canaan
keyEvents.description: Jalam was born as the son of Esau and Oholibama in the land of Canaan, as part of Esau's growing family.

keyEvents.title: Esau's sons listed
keyEvents.description: Jalam is mentioned among Esau's sons who were born in Canaan and formed the core of the Edomite people.

keyEvents.title: Jalam becomes a tribal chief
keyEvents.description: Jalam became one of the tribal chiefs (alufim) descended from Esau's wife Oholibama, leading his own tribe in Edom.

keyEvents.title: Esau's family moves from Canaan
keyEvents.description: Esau took his entire family, including Jalam, and moved away from his brother Jacob to the Seir mountains because the land could not support them both.

keyEvents.title: The ancestors of Edom in 1 Chronicles
keyEvents.description: Jalam is mentioned again in the genealogies of Chronicles as part of Esau's descendants and Edomite patriarchs.
